_comment: EXTERNAL composite-signature vectors. Produced by OTHER implementations, not by this engine.
WHY: on 2026-08-17 this engine signed the classical half of every composite certificate with
SHA-512 instead of the profile's draft-composite-sigs section 6 'Traditional Signature Algorithm'.
The engine's signer and verifier both read the same profile table, so every in-house round-trip
passed while the output was non-interoperable. No self-generated test could catch that class of
DO NOT regenerate these locally - a self-produced vector re-creates exactly the blind spot this
file exists to close. Refresh only by pulling a newer upstream round, deliberately.

5 certificate vectors (.37/.39/.40/.41/.48) and 1 raw vector (.40) added 2026-08-23, ported from pqctoday-hub's already-extracted third-party sources (Bouncy Castle / IETF Hackathon composite-sigs-ref-impl / IETF draft-19 Appendix E) at src/components/PKILearning/modules/HybridCrypto/data/externalVectors.ts -- mechanical base64-to-hex re-encoding of the SAME bytes, not a local regeneration.

raw_signature_vectors._note: NORMATIVE - published by the draft, produced by the reference implementation beside the draft source. No certificate encoding involved: public key, signature, fixed message.
raw_signature_vectors.message_utf8: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

vectors.label: COMPSIG-MLDSA87-ECDSA-P384-SHA512
vectors._note: HIGH-S regression case. This vector's ECDSA signature has a high S value. The hub's TypeScript verifier rejected it until 2026-08-18 because @noble/curves enforces low-S by default - a Bitcoin/Ethereum malleability convention that X.509, RFC 3279 and FIPS 186 do NOT require. This engine accepted it correctly. The disagreement between our own two implementations is what exposed the hub bug, which would have rejected roughly half of all valid third-party composite certificates.

vectors.label: COMPSIG-MLDSA44-ECDSA-P256-SHA256
vectors._note: P-256 / SHA-256. PH and traditional hash are the same here.

certificate_vectors._note: Bouncy Castle self-signed trust anchor. Independent producer; exercises the full Validate path.

vectors._note: PH=SHA256 AND traditional=SHA256 - the CONTROL profile. An implementation that wrongly uses PH as the traditional hash still passes here, so this vector isolates the mismatch cases above. Second producer, distinct from Bouncy Castle.

RSA-PSS classical half, and the only external vector that exercises the RSA path at all: it pins the draft §4.1 tradPK encoding (a bare DER RSAPublicKey, not an SPKI), the §6.1 Table 2 PSS parameters (SHA-256 + MGF1-SHA-256, 32-byte salt), and the §6 "RSA size: 2048" check. Note this is the RSA CONTROL case, exactly as .40 is for ECDSA: PH and the PSS hash are both SHA-256, so it cannot distinguish Table 2 from "reuse PH" - see the .41 gap noted in EXTERNAL_VECTOR_COVERAGE_GAPS.

vectors.producer: IETF draft-19 Appendix E reference vectors
vectors._note: Ed25519 classical half. Pins two readings that had NO outside witness until 2026-08-18: that tradPK is a bare 32-byte RFC 8410 key rather than an SPKI, and that Ed25519 signs M' directly as PureEdDSA rather than a pre-hashed digest (Ed25519ph). The Bouncy Castle r5 and IETF Hackathon composite-sigs-ref-impl copies of this profile were verified against this code at the same time and also pass, so three independent producers agree.

vectors.producer: IETF draft-19 Appendix E reference vectors
vectors._note: The highest-value vector in this file: the RSA analogue of F17. PH is SHA-512 while draft 6.1 Table 2 fixes the RSASSA-PSS hash at SHA-256, so an implementation that wrongly reuses PH as the PSS hash passes .37 (where both are SHA-256) and fails ONLY here. Until this vector landed the Table 2 reading rested on draft text alone. Also pins the section 6 'RSA size: 3072' check. Bouncy Castle r5 and the Hackathon ref-impl copies were verified at the same time and also pass.

vectors.producer: IETF draft-19 Appendix E reference vectors
vectors._note: Ed25519 at ML-DSA-65. Shares the Ed25519 handling with .39, so the two together guard the same readings at both parameter sets. Bouncy Castle r5 and Hackathon ref-impl copies verified at the same time and also pass.
